sourcedFrom: 990™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 107251, typeset 11/18/25 (2025)
cleanIntro: The 990 is a gas autoloader and gas guns fail dirty rather than worn. Its front end is the part that differs from every other Mossberg auto: a two-screw barrel clamp, a threaded magazine tube sleeve, and a handguard band that has to leave the forearm before the forearm leaves the tube. Empty the magazine tube before the chamber — the shells come out one at a time under spring pressure.

steps.title: Safety fully rearward, nothing on the trigger
steps.action: Push the safety button on the tang fully back to ON, keep the muzzle somewhere harmless, and keep fingers and objects off the trigger until the gun is proven empty.
steps.quote: Set the safety button fully rearward to the “ON” (SAFE) position. During unloading, never allow your fingers or any other object to contact the trigger.
steps.cite: 990™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 107251, typeset 11/18/25 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM

steps.title: ⛔ Magazine tube FIRST, chamber last
steps.action: Turn the gun trigger-guard-up and empty the tube before you touch the operating handle. Racking first only feeds another shell out of a full tube, and people who work chamber-first end up cycling a loaded gun repeatedly.
steps.quote: First, remove the shotshells from the magazine tube.
steps.cite: 990™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 107251, typeset 11/18/25 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM

steps.title: Elevator down, shell stop — one at a time, under spring
steps.action: Hold the elevator down with your thumb, then press and release the shell stop. One shell comes out under spring pressure — expect force and have a hand ready. Repeat until nothing more comes.
steps.quote: While holding the elevator down with your thumb, press and release the shell stop (Figure 8). This will release one shotshell from the magazine tube under spring pressure.
steps.cite: 990™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 107251, typeset 11/18/25 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM

steps.title: Now the chamber, and check all three places
steps.action: With the tube empty, turn the gun trigger-guard-down and pull the operating handle fully rearward to eject the chambered round. Then check chamber, elevator and magazine tube by eye and by finger — the elevator is the one people skip.
steps.quote: Lock the action open, visually and physically check the chamber, elevator, and magazine tube to ensure the firearm is completely unloaded
steps.cite: 990™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 107251, typeset 11/18/25 — DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: Eye protection — spatter and sprung parts
steps.action: Glasses on before the front end comes apart. There is an action spring in this gun that the book calls out by name.
steps.quote: Wear eye protection during disassembly and cleaning to protect your eyes from oil spatter or spring loaded components.
steps.cite: 990™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 107251, typeset 11/18/25 — DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: Barrel clamp off — 5/32" allen, both sides
steps.action: With the action locked open, take the two barrel clamp screws out with a 5/32" allen key, one each side, and lift the two halves of the clamp away. Note which way round they sat before they go in a tray.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel clamp. Using a 5/32” allen key to remove the screws (one each side). Remove the two halves of the barrel clamp. Note orientation for re-assembly.
steps.cite: 990™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 107251, typeset 11/18/25 — BARREL REMOVAL

steps.title: Magazine tube sleeve off
steps.action: Unscrew the magazine tube sleeve. This is a sleeve, not a cap — the 990's tube is threaded differently from the Aftershock's.
steps.cite: 990™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 107251, typeset 11/18/25 — BARREL REMOVAL

steps.title: ⛔ Forearm forward, and the HANDGUARD BAND comes off half way
steps.action: Slide the forearm forward, and once it is about half way down the tube slide the handguard band rearward off the forearm. Then continue forward until the forearm is free. Missing the band is the mistake the book warns about — it binds at the end of the tube with the forearm already past the point of easy recovery.
steps.quote: Once halfway down the magazine tube, remove the handguard band by sliding it rearward off the forearm assembly.
steps.cite: 990™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 107251, typeset 11/18/25 — BARREL REMOVAL

steps.title: ⛔ Leave the slide on the magazine tube
steps.action: Mossberg's own recommendation, and it is worth taking: keep the slide assembly on the tube while you clean. The action spring is under considerable pressure and reassembling it off the tube is the fiddly part.
steps.aside: The action spring is under considerable pressure.
steps.quote: It is recommended to keep the slide assembly on the magazine tube when disassembling and cleaning for easier reassembly.
steps.cite: 990™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 107251, typeset 11/18/25 — ACTION REMOVAL/DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: Operating handle straight out, bolt closed
steps.action: With the bolt closed, pull the operating handle straight out of the bolt assembly. Straight — levering it bends the shank.
steps.quote: Ensure the bolt is closed. Pull the operating handle straight out of the bolt assembly (Figure 13).
steps.cite: 990™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 107251, typeset 11/18/25 — ACTION REMOVAL/DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: Bolt, slide and piston stop out through the barrel opening
steps.action: Press the bolt release and slide the bolt assembly, slide assembly and piston stop out of the receiver through the barrel opening, leaving them on the magazine tube. Then lift the bolt off the slide.
steps.quote: While pressing the bolt release, slide out the bolt assembly, slide assembly and piston stop from the receiver through the opening for the barrel, leaving them on the magazine tube.
steps.cite: 990™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 107251, typeset 11/18/25 — ACTION REMOVAL/DISASSEMBLY

deepAbsentReason: The 990 book stops the owner at the action group in its own words — "No further disassembly is required" — and assigns anything beyond to an authorized Product Service Center. ⛔ No deeper path is invented for it.

cleaning.name: GAS SYSTEM — what decides whether it cycles
tasks: Solvent and a brass brush on the piston and the gas cylinder
Clear the gas ports; carbon here is why an autoloader short-strokes
Light oil then wipe back — oil in a gas system collects carbon
Note the order parts came off before anything goes back
cleaning.quote: Wear eye protection during disassembly and cleaning to protect your eyes from oil spatter or spring loaded components.
cleaning.src: 990™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual, DISASSEMBLY

cleaning.name: BARREL, BOLT AND RECEIVER
tasks: Bore and chamber with solvent, patches until clean
Bolt face, extractor and locking recesses
Wipe the magazine tube where the slide rides
Chokes out and threads cleaned before it is put away
cleaning.quote: Lock the action open, visually and physically check the chamber, elevator, and magazine tube to ensure the firearm is completely unloaded
cleaning.src: 990™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual, DISASSEMBLY

reassembly: Safety ON. Bolt onto the slide, both back into the receiver through the barrel opening, slide left on the magazine tube.
Operating handle pushed straight into the bolt.
Barrel on, seated fully into the receiver.
Forearm onto the tube, HANDGUARD BAND slid back on at the half-way point.
Magazine tube sleeve on, then both halves of the barrel clamp in the orientation you noted, 5/32" screws even.
Function test before it is put away.
fncheck: Safety ON, muzzle safe, chamber elevator and tube proven empty. Lock the bolt back and release it several times — it should run into battery and lock each time. Safety ON, pull the trigger: no hammer fall. Safety off, finger clear: no fall on its own; then the trigger drops it. ⛔ If the action does not lock open or the bolt will not close fully, suspect the gas system or a barrel not seated before you suspect anything else.
